stories.title: Gartner Names Context Graphs the Foundational Infrastructure Layer for Enterprise AI Agents (September 2026)
stories.body: In its September 15, 2026 report 'Context Graphs Ground AI Agents With Enterprise Knowledge,' Gartner identifies context graphs — combining declarative, procedural, and causal knowledge with runtime policy enforcement — as the essential layer that makes AI agents reliable at enterprise scale. Gartner separately named AI context platforms a Top Strategic Technology Trend for 2027 in a report published October 16, 2026, defining them as software that constructs, governs, and delivers semantically organized knowledge to agents. By 2028, Gartner predicts over 50% of AI agent systems will rely on context graphs, yet fewer than 10% of enterprises have a context layer today.
stories.why: This is Gartner naming your architecture — context layers, knowledge graphs, ontologies — as the mandatory pre-condition for agents that work. Every enterprise retail prospect running an agent pilot without a context layer is in the 42% cohort Gartner says reports AI costs exceeding value; this report is your proof point for why pilots stall and why data foundation comes first.

stories.title: McKinsey State of AI 2026: 32% of Enterprises Skipped a Software Purchase to Build In-House — But EBIT Impact Stayed Flat
stories.body: McKinsey's August 25, 2026 'State of AI: On the Road to ROI' survey of 1,719 organizations across 97 countries found that 32% had decided against buying at least one software product or feature because they could build it in-house with agentic coding tools — rising to nearly half among AI high performers. Despite this build surge, the share of respondents attributing any EBIT impact to AI stayed flat at 37%, unchanged from 2025, and only 6% qualify as true 'high performers' attributing 5%+ of EBIT to AI. Among large enterprises (over $1B revenue), 40% are now scaling AI agents in at least one function, up from 27% the prior year, while one in five organizations say AI operating costs are already constraining their AI use.
stories.why: The 'we'll build it ourselves' objection now has a McKinsey data rebuttal: building is surging but EBIT impact is flat, meaning self-builds are producing productivity theater, not margin. Use this to reframe build-vs-buy conversations with CIOs: the 6% who actually extract EBIT are the ones with governed data foundations, not the ones who skipped the platform.

stories.title: Sierra Raises $350M at $10B Valuation, Announces Retail Agents Now Reach Over 90% of Americans
stories.body: Sierra announced a $350M funding round led by Greenoaks at a $10B valuation and disclosed that its retail AI agents now reach over 90% of Americans via deployments with consumer brands. Sierra's Agent OS is designed to empower both customer experience teams and developers to build enterprise AI agents, with the company reporting well over $200M in annualized revenue as of August 2026 per a source close to the company. Competitor Decagon, valued at $4.5B after its January 2026 Series D, launched Voice 3 and a Personal Agent Gateway in October 2026 and became a launch partner on OpenAI's B2B marketplace, where enterprise OpenAI customers can apply existing commitments toward Decagon.
stories.why: Sierra's retail reach claim ('90% of Americans') and Decagon's OpenAI marketplace placement are competitive signals your prospects will see — understanding their pricing models (Sierra: outcome-based, unpublished; Decagon: per-conversation, unpublished) and architecture trade-offs lets you position where a context/data layer sits beneath or beside these agents. Neither vendor solves the data-foundation problem; that is the opening.

stories.title: BCG Report (Oct 21, 2026): AI Shopping Agents Threaten Retail's Digital Flywheel — 96% of Retailers Now Exploring Agent Formats
stories.body: BCG's October 21, 2026 report 'How Retailers Can Reinvent the Digital Flywheel for Agentic Commerce,' based on a survey of 50 leading retailers and 100 global brands, finds that AI shopping agents are beginning to reshape online retail and threaten the traffic engine that powers marketplaces, loyalty programs, and retail media. Among retailers that have already upgraded retail media capabilities, 65% report better campaign performance and 40% report higher retail media pricing. BCG's broader AI Radar (2,400 business executives) finds four out of five CEOs are more optimistic about AI ROI than a year ago and nearly all CEOs believe AI agents will produce measurable returns in 2026.
stories.why: This is BCG putting a named research stake in the ground that agentic commerce disrupts the entire retail digital flywheel — not just customer service. For a sales conversation, it frames urgency: retailers who wait on agent infrastructure lose the data signals that make personalization, media, and loyalty work, which is exactly the downstream consequence of poor context-layer investment.

stories.title: BCG: Agentic AI in CPG–Retailer Supply Chains Delivers +2–4% In-Stock Improvement and 60%+ Planning Productivity Gains
stories.body: BCG's supply chain report documents that agentic AI deployed at the CPG–retailer interface — with agents continuously monitoring store- and DC-level inventory against sell-through velocity and proactively pushing replenishment before a retailer's own cycle catches a trending out-of-stock — can boost in-stocks by 2–4% and planning productivity by over 60%. The report notes that out-of-stocks remain stubbornly at 5–10% even for high-velocity SKUs despite years of data-sharing, and that a global CPG leader redesigned its replenishment workflow using an agentic platform as a case example. BCG's May 2026 executive perspectives report also found that 69% of executives say agentic AI requires entirely new governance and measurement frameworks.
stories.why: This is the closest item to a named enterprise outcome in supply chain — the exact workflow (replenishment, ordering, CPG-retailer collaboration) that Graas operates in. The 2–4% in-stock lift and 60% planning productivity figure are proof-point numbers you can put in a deck; the governance gap (69% say they need new frameworks) is the opening for a context-layer conversation about why agents need governed data before they can act.
